name: belts-tick
conditions: Tyler's Mac (Apple M3 Max), native release (cargo test --release), fx-belts' standard belt world at genesis (M40's Mixed regime, seed 7: 3,810 lines, 50,000 belt tiles, 1,090 spawners; since M53 (0079 §21) each spawner sets its line's schedule once and the engine performs the inserts in advance, so the spawner entities are never written and the eight frames a tick carry only structure changes and section 13: 107 B of frames a tick, where M47b-M52 measured 53,501-54,153 B of entity deltas; caps 32,768 lines and 393,216 items, so the item cap never binds) through packages/engine/fixtures/belts/tests/bench_belts.rs: Host<Belts> with 8 connections holding maximum views (256 x 256 tiles, stacked over the 220 x 545-tile world), unpaced, production hashing, no actions; 200 warm-up ticks then 1,200 measured; a tick is admit + seal + tick + build_frame x 8, frames discarded. The tick phase holds 1,090 no-op visits of the spawner entities on the "spawner" list (a known cost, brief 53's Deviations). Promoted with pnpm bench:baseline from the manager's median gate run of M53 (pnpm test:slow rust -t slow_tick_belts_large) on 2026-10-12, three runs at 1-min load under 4: 0.2203 / 0.2125 / 0.2146 ms (tick 0.120-0.123, advance 0.063-0.065, frames 0.095-0.098) at 1-min/5-min load 1.73-3.35 / 4.94-4.99 (19:33-19:35 PDT), the median run 3 promoted; an earlier set on the same tree read 0.2129 / 0.2130 / 0.2308; down from M47b's 1.2638 ms because the frames phase measured the fixture's entity deltas (about 1.0 ms of the 1.26) and the tick phase their writes; the gate's 25 % rule and the 5 ms limit stand.
